English: Sand Pit Well
A simple, hand-dug pit in the sand, providing the most basic access to groundwater for the faithful.
Stone Lined Well
A more permanent well, reinforced with stone lining, protecting water from collapse and contamination.
Covered Well
A well protected by a wooden cover and partial shelter, keeping the water clean and sacred.
Draw Well
A sophisticated well with a pulley and bucket system, enabling easier access to the life-giving waters for monks and travelers.
Oasis Enclosure
A fortified enclosure built around the well, offering protection for pilgrims and securing the sacred waters.
Deep Shaft Well
A masterfully dug deep shaft well, reaching pure underground water and symbolizing the depth of faith.
Desert Cistern
A vast underground cistern, storing water for dry seasons and allowing for greater gatherings and spiritual study.
Walled Water Source
Massive stone walls encircle the well, transforming it into a shrine and safe haven for the devout.
Shaded Wellhouse
A large, domed structure built over the well and cistern, providing shelter for worshippers and attracting desert scholars.
Desert Water Sanctuary
A grand sanctuary enclosing the sacred well, with marble colonnades, gardens, and space for great religious councils. A marvel of faith and desert survival.
